headline: Sajek Valley reopens to tourists after 4-day closure for Durga Puja
summary: The popular tourist destination in Rangamati was closed for an indefinite period but has now been reopened. The road blockade for the festival has also been suspended.
details: Sajek Valley, a popular tourist spot in Baghaichhari Upazila of Rangamati, has been reopened to tourists after being closed for four days. The district administration issued an urgent public notice on Thursday night announcing the reopening of all tourist centers in Sajek Valley.
The decision to reopen comes after a previous notice on October 11 that had indefinitely suspended all tourist activities. Tourists who were present in Sajek were instructed to leave by October 13.

The reopening coincides with the suspension of a six-day road blockade program in Sajek, which was scheduled to protest the Sharadiya Durga Puja festival. The blockade has been suspended from October 16 to October 21, allowing for smoother travel during the festive period.
caption:
Good news for travelers! Sajek Valley is now open for tourists after a four-day closure. The road blockade for Durga Puja has also been suspended.

Sajek Valley, a popular tourist spot in Baghaichhari Upazila of Rangamati, has been reopened to tourists after being closed for four days. The district administration issued an urgent public notice on Thursday night announcing the reopening of all tourist centers in Sajek Valley.

The decision to reopen comes after a previous notice on October 11 that had indefinitely suspended all tourist activities. Tourists who were present in Sajek were instructed to leave by October 13.

The reopening coincides with the suspension of a six-day road blockade program in Sajek, which was scheduled to protest the Sharadiya Durga Puja festival. The blockade has been suspended from October 16 to October 21, allowing for smoother travel during the festive period.

topic: measles outbreak continues with new deaths
headline_marked: Measles outbreak: [[1,181 deaths]] recorded as four more die in 24 hours
headline: Measles outbreak: 1,181 deaths recorded as four more die in 24 hours
summary: The country's confirmed and suspected measles death toll has surpassed 1,181 this year, with four new fatalities reported in the last 24 hours. The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) confirmed these latest deaths as suspected measles cases.
details: Four more patients have died with measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours until 8:00am today, pushing the country’s combined tally of confirmed and suspected measles-related deaths to 1,181 this year. The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) classified all four latest fatalities as suspected measles deaths.

With these recent deaths, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 1,077, while confirmed deaths from measles remain unchanged at 104. A total of 1,306 new suspected measles cases were reported during the same 24-hour period, bringing the cumulative nationwide total to 209,876.

In addition, 86 new confirmed measles cases were recorded, taking the total number of laboratory-confirmed infections to 22,926. Since March 15 this year, a total of 186,583 patients with suspected measles have been hospitalised across the country, with 178,869 having recovered, according to the DGHS.
